key: Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven.
s: After a plea not to suffer for another’s sin, the hymn to the Universal Gods praises reverence itself; Sāyaṇa, on 6.51.8, reads homage as mightiest because all is won by it, and heaven and earth as lasting long because creatures revere them.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.51.8, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 200162 (2019)

opened.locator: commentary on 6.51.8, and the hymn introduction

evidence.words: “नम “इत् नमस्कार एव “उग्रम् उद्गूर्णबलं सर्वोत्कृष्टम् । तेन हि सर्वं लभ्यते । अतः “नमः नमस्कारम् “आ “विवासे परिचरामि । “नमः नमस्कार एव “पृथिवीमुत “द्यां द्युलोकं च “दाधार धारयति । द्यावापृथिव्यौ प्राणिभिर्नमस्क्रियमाणे सत्यौ तदुपभोगाय चिरकालमवतिष्ठेते ।
evidence.gloss: Homage alone is mighty, of raised strength, highest of all; for by it everything is obtained. Therefore I serve homage. Homage itself upholds earth and heaven: heaven and earth, being revered by living beings, remain for a long time for their use.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 6.51.8, at [491,8]), the first two whole sentences of the unit, no dash. Sāyaṇa on 6.51.8 glosses ugram as uplifted strength, highest of all, because by homage everything is obtained, and says heaven and earth, being revered by living beings, endure a long time for their enjoyment; Wilson note 2 reports the scholiast the same way. Hymn introduction confirms a vaiśvadeva hymn (Universal Gods). Plain sense faithful: 6.51.7 is the plea not to suffer for the sin of others; no four words of the key repeated. Revision 200162 dated 2019-04-24 by the Wikisource API, so the src year stands. Evidence found verbatim in packet output. entry-check ok.
